comparison: Both evaluate claims about parallel QC systems (C6, C31, C89-C93, C139) based on Figure 6 genetic interaction data. OpenEval finds the synthetic phenotypes convincingly demonstrate parallel function. Peer reviewers raise concerns about lack of specificity in genetic interactions (Δart1 interacts with multiple genes) and inadequate quantitative analysis, stating 'this section needs to be strengthened or the figure should be removed.'

Both evaluate Lyp1 toxicity claims (C79-C88) based on promoter titrations, ubiquitination mutants, and PI staining. Both find the evidence convincing that PM protein accumulation is toxic and Art1-mediated clearance is protective. Strong agreement on this set of claims.

Both evaluate claims about cargo accumulation causing toxicity and PM clearance providing protection (C4-C5, C28-C29, C58-C61, C121-C122). Both find the PI staining and viability data convincing. Peer reviewers describe this as 'exciting' work documenting consequences when the mechanism fails. Strong agreement despite OpenEval noting the molecular mechanism remains speculative.

Both evaluate the central conclusion that ART-Rsp5 functions as a PMQC system (C3, C99, C149). OpenEval finds collective evidence from all experiments supports this. Peer reviewers accept the core claim, describing the work as showing 'how the ubiquitin-driven endocytosis machinery surveys the plasma membrane for defective proteins.' Strong agreement on the fundamental conclusion.

Both address heat-induced cargo trafficking (C25, C32-C33 overlap). OpenEval finds microscopy and Western blot evidence convincing. Peer reviewers raise critical concern that PM signal doesn't obviously decrease in some cases, suggesting heat may trigger TGN sorting rather than endocytosis. Reviewers request control experiments to rule out this alternative explanation.

Partial overlap on Rsp5 requirement claims (C51-C52, C103). OpenEval finds genetic data convincing for Rsp5's role in heat-induced endocytosis. Peer reviewers' uncertainty about whether trafficking is truly endocytic (vs. TGN sorting) indirectly affects interpretation of Rsp5's role, though they don't directly challenge the Rsp5 requirement data.

Both evaluate misfolding/aggregation evidence (C44-C45, C47-C48, C101). OpenEval finds detergent solubility and sucrose gradient data convincing. Peer reviewers do not challenge these biochemical findings, and their positive overall assessment suggests acceptance of the misfolding evidence.

Both address thermostability and mechanistic interpretation (C35-C37, C42). OpenEval finds differential thermostability data and temperature-folding relationship interpretation well-supported. Peer reviewers do not challenge thermostability findings or glycerol stabilization data, suggesting acceptance.

Both evaluate glycerol stabilization evidence (C39, C41). OpenEval finds this supports misfolding recognition. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, and lack of critique combined with positive assessment suggests acceptance of the glycerol stabilization data.

Both address cargo-specific misfolding recognition (C26, C102). OpenEval finds aggregation, thermostability, and glycerol data support this. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, suggesting acceptance of the cargo-specific recognition evidence.

Both evaluate claims about PM clearance being protective (C59-C61). OpenEval finds genetic dissection of endocytic vs. post-endocytic mutations convincing. Peer reviewers accept the PI staining data and protection conclusions without challenge. Agreement on the critical role of PM clearance.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive ART network data (C64-C75) including genetic screens, redundancy, and synthetic phenotypes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim group, though peer reviewers accept the overall PMQC conclusion.
OpenEval identifies speculative claims about toxicity mechanism (C30, C62, C123-C126) as unsupported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic speculations.

OpenEval finds claims about disordered regions and aggregation recognition (C115-C119) uncertain due to lack of experimental testing of functional role. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these structural/mechanistic claims.

OpenEval finds Art1 activation mechanism claims (C131-C134) uncertain due to reliance on unpublished negative results and incomplete understanding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic details.
OpenEval identifies broader implications and future applications (C135-C138, C143, C152) as unsupported speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these extrapolations.
OpenEval identifies mammalian ARRDC speculation (C150-C151) as unsupported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these translational hypotheses.
